item.title: Red Wings Fans Enraged Over Captaincy Plan
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings have a captaincy problem, and judging by the latest reactions on social media, some fans are running out of patience with how the organization is handling it. With former captain Dylan Larkin no longer wearing the “C” following his offseason trade request, Detroit has chosen, according to Todd McLellan , to move forward without naming a replacement. The organization previously announced that a permanent decision would be left to its next hockey operations leader, but that approach is drawing criticism from fans who believe the answer is already standing in the Red Wings’ locker room. And that answer, according to several frustrated supporters, is Moritz Seider. This org is a fkn dumpster fire!” Another fan, Revelator42 (@foardeetou), offered a much more detailed criticism of the decision to make Larkin captain in the first place. “Wings gave Dylan Larkin the C in the hopes that he would grow into it. item.title: ‘He’s a coward. He can’t coach’: Dave Portnoy demands apology after being ‘right about Ryan Day from the jump’
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It was a rough weekend for Michigan, as the Wolverines lost to rival Michigan State and fired their offensive coordinator. But Barstool Sports founder and devoted Michigan fan Dave Portnoy still found something to celebrate. Ohio State suffered a blowout loss of its own, falling to Oregon for its second straight defeat. And Portnoy, who has been a longtime critic of Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day, said he’s owed an apology from every Ohio State fan in Columbus. Portnoy’s Feud With Ryan Day Portnoy has been one of Day’s harshest critics for years, and things have only gotten more personal this season. In August, he called Day a “scared little chicken-boy” after Ohio State moved its senior day from the Michigan game to Week 1. Then in October, Barstool was removed from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff , and Portnoy blamed Day for the decision. “I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy sh*t even I didnt realize he was this soft,” Portnoy wrote on X at the time, calling the Buckeyes coach “Cryin Ryan.” Awful Announcing noted that the breakup was always inevitable . A couple of weeks later, Portnoy said that Day “would be unsuccessful at any program other than Ohio State.” “Ryan Day was born on third base,” Portnoy said. “Like, anybody here could coach that team to 10, 11 wins.” This weekend gave Portnoy plenty of new material. Michigan fell 15-6 to Michigan State, and the Wolverines fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, whom Portnoy had called “horrific.” But Ohio State blew a 14-0 lead in a 41-28 loss to Oregon, its second straight defeat, and Day said afterward that “there needs to be accountability” for the team’s struggles. ‘He’s a coward’ On Monday’s episode of Wake Up Barstool , Portnoy made it clear that he was enjoying Ohio State’s struggles. “I want an apology from every single person in Columbus. I want them to get in line and line up,” Portnoy said, in a clip shared by the show . “I want them all to come in a receiving line and say, ‘Hey, Dave Portnoy, you’ve been right about Ryan Day from the jump. He’s a coward. He can’t coach. He was born on third base.’ All of it. Get in line and say, ‘I’m sorry, you should be back on Big Noon Kickoff . It was a joke what they did to you,'” he continued. Portnoy admitted that Michigan has problems of its own, but he said that Ohio State’s situation is even worse given the talent on the roster. “Yes, we have problems in Ann Arbor, but that team’s a joke with the talent they have. So yeah, real bad weekend for Michigan, no doubt,” Portnoy said. “But let’s not forget, as bad as a weekend Michigan had, Michigan State had a worse weekend, and Ohio State had the worst weekend of the bunch.” Needless to say, Portnoy is going to enjoy every minute of this before The Game. item.title: AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars make bold move, trading for Falcons safety Jessie Bates III
item.description: Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III (3) and Xavier Watts (31) celebrate after Bates III intercepted a San Francisco 49ers' Brock Purdy pass during the second half of an NFL football game in Atlanta, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (AP Photo/Brynn Anderson) (Brynn Anderson/Associated Press) The Jacksonville Jaguars took a big swing a day before the NFL trade deadline , grabbing All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons on Monday morning, according to multiple reports . The Jaguars (6-2), who are just a half-game behind the Buffalo Bills and Denver Broncos for best record in the AFC and have a three-game lead over the Houston Texans in the AFC South, are giving up a second-round pick in next year's NFL draft and a fifth-rounder in 2028. By comparison, the Texans gave up a second- and seventh-rounder in exchange for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick last month. Bates, who will turn 30 years old in February, is in the final year of a four-year, $64 million contract and is still playing well. The former second-round pick out of Wake Forest, made the Pro Bowl in 2023 and was second-team All-Pro last season. Bates, who has made 61 straight starts and hasn't missed a game since 2022, also was second-team All-Pro in 2020 and 2023. "Woke up a Jaguar!," Bates posted on Twitter on Monday morning. The Jaguars had an urgent need at safety ever since former Texans defensive back Eric Murray was lost for the season due to an elbow he injury he suffered against the Colts last week. Murray, who left the Texans for a three-year, $19.5 million contract with Jacksonville following the 2024 season, had started 17 games for the Jaguars over the past two seasons before the injury. The Jaguars' defense ranks second in the league, giving up just 15.1 points per game, but they have been vulnerable through the air. Jacksonville ranks 22nd in pass defense, allowing 229 passing yards per game. When the Texans beat Jacksonville 34-31 in London last month, C.J. Stroud threw for 312 yards and three touchdowns. The Texans and Jaguars meet again on Dec. 20 at Reliant Stadium. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Mowbray's 'soldiers and artists' march up the table
item.description: [BBC] Since the lengthy international break across September and October, Blackburn Rovers have taken 12 points from a possible 21. That is a healthy return by any measure. The only real blemish was the 4-0 hammering at Swansea City , a day on which Rovers never turned up. Beyond that, there has been plenty to like. With just over a third of the season gone, it feels like the perfect moment to take stock. Most importantly, Rovers are looking up, not down. Twelve months ago, supporters were nervously checking the bottom end of the table. Now the conversation is about the play-offs. That alone tells you how much has changed. And it's about more than points. Ewood Park feels alive again. That revival began under Michael O'Neill, but Tony Mowbray has kept the momentum going. Matchdays feel like events once more. The big away followings have helped. Not many clubs can hand over more than 7,000 tickets to travelling supporters, and fans have responded in numbers. Crowds nudging 20,000 for games against Middlesbrough, Coventry City, Leicester City and West Ham over the past seven months have brought a buzz back to the place. The only defeat among them came in a dead-rubber against an already relegated Leicester side. The positivity extends beyond the stands. Most of this squad bears the scars of last season's struggles. Apart from Sam Morsy, Jayden Fevrier and Gady Beyuku, these players have lived through difficult times at Ewood. Yet they look liberated rather than burdened by the experience. That's where the Mowbray factor comes in. His "soldiers and artists" philosophy sounds simple, but right now it's working a treat. The artists are thriving. Todd Cantwell and Dapo Afolayan have become central figures. Both have stayed fit. Both along with centre back Sean McLoughlin are ever-presents. Both are proving they can be difference-makers. That's a far cry from last season. Afolayan managed just one start after his February arrival and was hooked at half-time. Cantwell started fewer than half of Rovers' league games and never really had the freedom to express himself. This team is playing with far more adventure, which suits both players perfectly. Anyone familiar with Mowbray's career should not be surprised. For all his reputation as a no-nonsense centre-half, his teams have always tried to attack. That's in his DNA. It always has been. Then there are the soldiers. Morsy remains the heartbeat of the side. Mowbray calls him his coach on the pitch and it is easy to understand why. His influence seems to be rubbing off on academy graduate Kristi Montgomery, who looks increasingly comfortable at Championship level. Together, they give Rovers a solid foundation. The next phase of the season now feels crucial. There are 24 league matches and at least one FA Cup tie before the next international break. item.description: Manchester City's Marc Guéhi has been forced to withdraw from England's latest camp through injury -Credit:Justin Setterfield, Getty Images Dan Burn has been called up to England's squad following Marc Guéhi's withdrawal due to injury. The Newcastle United defender received the call for the UEFA Nations League double-header after Guéhi was ruled out with a hip problem. Manchester City's Guéhi was substituted at halftime during his side's loss at Nottingham Forest and subsequently underwent scans, leading to his withdrawal, with the remainder of the squad reporting for duty at Tottenham Hotspur's training facility on Monday. It is a welcome development for Burn, who played a significant role in England's FIFA World Cup run before missing out on the last two squads. Soccer star Jesús de Miguel tragically dies aged 30 after mid-game collision as tributes paid Premier League star prompts major police response after bow and arrow incident -Credit:Eurasia Sport Images, Getty Images England manager Thomas Tuchel stated on Friday that Burn remains in his plans, even as they focus on developing the next generation of players ahead of the 2028 Euros. Meanwhile, Tuchel confirmed that Jordan Pickford retains his status as first-choice goalkeeper, while acknowledging that James Trafford is pushing hard for the position. Pickford and Trafford could share goalkeeping duties across the fixtures against Croatia and Spain, mirroring the arrangement from the previous international window. "No, he is," Tuchel said on Pickford being first choice, via The Mirror . "But nothing has changed. The competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And Traff gets regular starts now, that's what we wanted. "James Trafford did well. They shared the matches last time. I'm not sure what we will do. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE "I have to speak with our goalkeeper coach. But the goalkeepers, they are a bit of a unit for themselves, and rightly so. "Yes, it's slightly different, but when do I have a chance to see another goalkeeper, if not in Nations League? If not in high-pressure matches? "So we had James against Spain, we asked ourselves is this fair for James Trafford to straightaway go against Spain, but I think it's exactly what we need. Because what happens if Jordan Pickford is injured? What happens if he's not available? So it's better to test it."

item.title: Cardinals' Budda Baker's stance on trade rumors revealed by NFL insider
item.description: Cardinals' Budda Baker's stance on trade rumors revealed by NFL insider originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals lost again in Week 9, and it's very obvious that they will be sellers at the NFL trade deadline. They've already traded Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jacoby Brissett this season. So, who's next? While the running back, tight end, and wide receiver rooms seem set, the Cardinals might trade from their defense. One player worth keeping an eye on is fan favorite safety Budda Baker. While the Cardinals might not want to trade him, ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler revealed that Baker would "welcome" a trade from the Cardinals this season to a contender. Budda Baker would 'welcome' a trade from Cardinals "My sense is Budda Baker would welcome a chance to play for a contender if AZ entertains talks (big if)," Fowler reports. While Fowler isn't reporting that the Cardinals are looking to trade Baker, or that Baker has requested a trade, it does reveal a trade is much more in play than it might've been in years past. Baker isn't opposed to being traded, especially if it's to a real contender. The Buffalo Bills would be a team to watch in the sweepstakes for the star safety. Arizona is in a rebuild, and trading a veteran player for a haul of draft picks would make sense. There's no guarantee Baker will be traded, but he is at least open to a trade. MORE : Jaguars reportedly acquiring Falcons' Pro Bowl safety in major trade Will the Cardinals actually trade Baker, though? It's hard to say that they will, as Fowler notes that the team entertaining trade offers is a "big if." A trade is possible, as the player would be open to a deal and Arizona has shown a willingness to trade key players this season. If they trade Baker, the trade of Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars , involving a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, is a good benchmark to hit. The Cardinals might be able to get more for Baker. That is, if they even trade him. A Baker trade is a huge hurdle to clear, and even if teams make strong offers, Arizona might decide to keep Baker. He and Josh Sweat are two big names to watch, but there's a very real possibility neither is dealt by the November 10 deadline. item.title: Miami Dolphins overreaction Monday: Listen to all trade deadline calls
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― The Miami Dolphins lost to the Detroit Lions 19-9 to fall to 1-7. Chris Johnson had his first career interception. Jacob Rodriguez had his first career sack. The Dolphins defense allowed only one touchdown and has shown impressive progress. It's never a bad time for an Overreaction Monday, so ... here goes. Malik Willis has not proven to be long-term answer Overreaction? No. As of Sunday night, Willis' NFL ranks were: passer rating (26th), passing yards (25th), passing TDs (24th) and yard per attempt (20th). He also is tied for the 8th-most interceptions in the league. That's not good enough and also below preseason expectations. There are reasons. There always are. Pressure. Young receivers. A few injuries that have hampered his running in recent games. But Willis has up to nine more games to show Miami they don't need to draft a first-round quarterback on April 29. Defense has 4 building blocks Overreaction? No. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez , linebacker Jordyn Brooks, cornerback Chris Johnson and defensive tackle Jordan Phillips are four defensive players good enough for any team to win with. We will see how things play out for Kenneth Grant, Trey Moore, Michael Taaffe, Kyle Louis, Dante Trader and others. Chop Robinson is a unique situation only because of five career concussions, which complicates matters of the future. But Miami's defense was strong against the Lions and there are some foundational pieces. Dolphins must consider all trade offers Overreaction? No. Miami must listen closely to any and all offers for players like Austin Jackson, Zach Sieler , Josh Uche, Jaylen Wright, JuJu Brents, etc. The Dolphins have no choice but to try to add a pick or two to help foster the dramatic rebuild. The deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. Eastern. Special teams among worst ever Overreaction? No. The Dolphins missed a field goal, had a botched kickoff and allowed a fake punt completion to the Lions. We can feel a little bit of empathy for veteran special teams coach Chris Tabor, who is working with a room of kindergartners. But it has to be better. After the last game, coach Jeff Hafley said Zane Gonzalez cannot miss a short kick before halftime that would have tied the score at 6. This has been hard to watch. Really hard. Dolphins headed for a Top 3 pick Overreaction? No. The Dolphins have upcoming games against the bad Colts, bad Jets and bad Chargers. Is a 4-13 finish possible? Sure. But a 3-14 finish is more probable. That would put Miami in the top two positions of the next NFL draft, which is helpful, considering Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith and Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker may be the top two picks. There are also pass rushers from Texas and South Carolina who will be in that mix. Top 4 is OK. Top 3 is better. Top 2 is ideal. item.title: Dan Campbell honors Jack Campbell with game ball after Lions' Miami win
item.description: View this post on Instagram A post shared by Detroit Lions (@detroitlionsnfl) The Detroit Lions ' celebration in Miami after their 19-9 win over the Dolphins quickly turned to injured captain Jack Campbell. After Sunday's win, coach Dan Campbell gave an emotional locker-room speech on Sunday, Nov. 8 about the team's resilience before announcing a game ball for Jack Campbell when the room erupted. “Yes, sir,” one player could be heard yelling. item.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson Becker has broken his silence regarding his long-term future at Anfield, expressing a clear desire to extend his stay on Merseyside. The Brazilian international, whose current deal is approaching its conclusion, remains a pivotal figure for the Reds as they navigate a new era under the current coaching staff. Alisson confirms desire for Anfield extension Speaking about his current mindset regarding a potential contract renewal, in quotes reported by BBC Sport , Alisson was incredibly transparent about where he sees himself playing in the coming years. 'Yes [I want to stay], in my mind. I'm focused on playing every game but in my mind I'm happy to stay,' said Alisson. The 34-year-old goalkeeper, who made a £66.8m switch from Roma in 2018 and has since amassed 347 appearances for the Reds, remains a fundamental figure at Anfield . The Brazilian further elaborated on the factors that will influence his final decision, though his personal preference is already set in stone. 'That depends on a lot of aspects and different situations. But my will is to stay - I'm happy here and my family is happy here,' he explained. 'I'm still hungry for titles and delivering good performances. I still want to play at the top level for as long as I can, so that's my thinking.' Contract negotiations and managerial backing When asked directly if he had engaged in formal talks over a new contract, the keeper clarified the current status of the situation. 'No, but my agent is talking with the club,' he revealed. The Brazilian has established a legendary status at Anfield, having won two Premier League titles, two League Cups, the FA Cup, the Champions League, and the Club World Cup during his time with the club. The goalkeeper's desire to stay aligns perfectly with the public stance taken by the Liverpool coaching staff. Last week, head coach Andoni Iraola addressed the uncertainty surrounding the veteran, admitting he was unsure if this would be the final chapter for the Brazilian but expressing a strong wish for him to remain part of the project. Iraola noted that he hoped the goalkeeper could 'continue for more time,' recognizing the immense value Alisson brings not just in terms of shot-stopping, but also in his leadership within the dressing room. Building consistency for a title charge Following a difficult week that saw Liverpool suffer setbacks against Arsenal and Fenerbahce, Alisson produced a series of crucial saves to help secure a vital victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday. 'Our reality is that we're not doing as well as we can. It doesn't mean that we are not doing well - we are doing well in so many games - but the consistency is not there yet,' he admitted.

item.description: Pau Cubarsí wins the 2026 Golden Boy award Pau Cubarsí now reigns supreme among world football’s young talents. The 19-year-old FC Barcelona centre-back has been named the winner of the 2026 Golden Boy award, presented annually by Italian newspaper Tuttosport since 2003 to recognise the most outstanding footballer under 21 playing in Europe’s leagues. The decision was officially announced early on Monday afternoon at a formal ceremony in the Italian town of Sassuolo. A milestone for defenders Cubarsí’s triumph marks a rare milestone in the award’s history: he is only the second centre-back to receive the honour in its more than two decades of existence, following in the footsteps of Dutchman Matthijs de Ligt in 2018. The roll of honour has otherwise traditionally been reserved for renowned forwards and playmakers such as Lionel Messi, Wayne Rooney, Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland and Jude Bellingham. Barça dominance and Spanish representation With this trophy, FC Barcelona extends its record at the top of the award’s all-time standings. Cubarsí joins Lionel Messi, Pedri, Gavi and Lamine Yamal as the five La Masia-trained players to have claimed the Golden Boy while wearing Barça’s colours. Cubarsí succeeds Désiré Doué (2025) and Lamine Yamal (2024), reaffirming Spanish football’s prominence in an edition whose nominees also included Jon Martín (Real Sociedad) and his teammates Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart. item.description: (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fourth-wave sports take culture has found a new frontier: the delay take. I could have ripped that the Chicago Bears were the Super Bowl favorite after their monstrous win over the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football, when I and the rest of the world saw Jeffrey Simmons and Montez Sweat go to town on the defending champs while Caleb Williams, D’Andre Swift and their army of pass catchers diced up Seattle’s vaunted defense like expert fugu sushi chefs who are specially trained to cut up pufferfish in a specific way so that instead of killing the person, it becomes a delicious delicacy. But I didn’t. I delayed the take until after one of the most ridiculous, out-of-control carnival explosions of a football game I’ve ever seen, and I’m still going to tell you the Chicago Bears should be Super Bowl favorites, because it’s still what I believe, it’s still what I saw on Sunday Night Football, and now? I think the take got a lot more interesting because Caleb Williams’ four interceptions against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the general drunkenness of that game gave us some glorious nuance to apply to the take. In five years, everyone will be doing delay takes. The Bears are not Super Bowl favorites, at least according to betting markets, though it’s a shockingly tight top four; on FanDuel, the Bears sit at 8 to 1 , trailing only the 49ers and Buffalo Bills, tied for top odds at 6 to 1. That’s one of the tighter betting ecosystems I can remember this far into the season, and reflects the lack of an assumed institutional favorite like the New England Patriots of old, the Kansas City Chiefs of less-old and the Los Angeles Rams of what-was-supposed-to-be-right-now. The Jacksonville Jaguars, who right before I started writing this traded for Jessie Bates III , are right on the Bears’ heels at +850. But I think Chicago should be ahead of Buffalo and San Francisco, even after Sunday’s fascinating exercise in seeing how many times you can turn the ball over and still win the game. The internet was ready and waiting to unload its worst insults on Drake Maye for his three interceptions against the Green Bay Packers in the Patriots’ blowout loss, but then Caleb decided to throw four and win, causing mass confusion. Most of that was because the Buccaneers never seriously threatened any kind of downfield passing game, and for Tampa Bay to win the turnover margin by three and lose suggests a total mismatch of offensive ability. The Bears couldn’t always move the ball when they needed to on Sunday night, but they could move it enough to overwhelm an opposing offense that just had nothing doing. item.title: Why Mercedes says a repeat of its 2014-2021 dominance is "impossible"
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin has argued that the Brackley outfit cannot expect to repeat its run of eight consecutive constructors' titles after its 2026 success. Mercedes clinched its ninth constructors' championship at Interlagos on Sunday, ending a wait that began after the last of those eight in 2021. The Toto Wolff-led team won every constructors' title from 2014 to 2021, a streak that ended just as F1 entered the ground-effect era in 2022, a year after the introduction of the budget cap. Red Bull and McLaren then took two titles each before this year's new regulations gave Mercedes an opportunity to return to the top. Shovlin joined F1 TV's post-race show in the middle of the celebrations. "I think one of the things that made us strong this year was that we hadn't been winning in the previous years," he explained. "You've got to look at it as, 'How are we going to beat ourselves next year? What are we going to do that would actually allow us to push forward and bring forward a better team?' Andrew Shovlin, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Andrew Shovlin, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes "It's difficult because it's tight. You've seen Ferrari have very strong races, McLaren today and Red Bull recently. But we will take nothing for granted. "I think to do the run that we did in the past of eight championships is really impossible with the way the sport is now, with the cost cap. But we'll try and do the same again. Work hard, assume you're going to get beaten if you don't do the best job, and we'll try and do the best job." As champion, Mercedes will get the least aerodynamic testing time, which Shovlin played down when asked about it. "It does peg you back, but it leads to exciting racing because it's harder to kind of dominate in the way that teams have in the past. But it's just something you've got to work around," he added. item.title: Arsenal monitor Leverkusen striker Kofane
item.description: Christian Kofane has score three goals in six appearances in all competitions so far this season for Bayer Leverkusen. [Getty Images] Arsenal have been monitoring Bayer Leverkusen striker Christian Kofane as they look at potential forward options to add to their ranks. The 20-year-old striker is currently out with a hamstring injury but has scored three goals in six games in all competitions this season for the German side. The forward will be familiar to Gunners fans as he was part of the Leverkusen team that played against Arsenal in the Champions League last season with Mikel Arteta's side winning 3-1 on aggregate in the last-16 stage. Arsenal wanted to sign a forward in the last transfer window and were unsuccessful in their attempts to bring in Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jnr and Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez, while they also had an interest in Morgan Rogers before the England international joined Chelsea. Kofane has had a fast rise, moving from AS Nylon in Cameroon to Albacete in 2024 where he scored eight goals in 20 games in La Liga 2. That scoring form saw him noticed by Leverkusen where he signed in July 2025. Since the move, the Cameroon international has scored 10 goals and registered nine assists in 50 games for Leverkusen in all competitions. Arsenal have had an excellent start to this season, winning nine of their 10 Premier League games. However, the Gunners' attacking play has been questioned with Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka the top scorers in the league with three goals each. Six of Arsenal's wins in the league have been by a single-goal margin and first choice forward Havertz has been caught offside 15 times this season - the most in the Premier League. Arsenal also have Viktor Gyokeres in their squad but the Swedish international, who scored 21 goals in all competitions during the last campaign, has been second choice to Havertz this season and has started just once in the league. Arteta said after the 1-0 win over Hull that his side need to be more "efficient" when through on goal and that he feels his players are "trying to score a perfect goal" against teams that defend in a low block.
